paragraphs: Swansea Council's fostering service is Foster Wales Swansea, one of the 22 local authority fostering teams that make up Foster Wales. It is a not-for-profit service, and when a Swansea child needs a foster home the council first looks to its own carers, turning to independent agencies such as those on this page when none of its carers is available. The council reports that 141 children were placed in foster care in 2023 to 2024, 30 of them with agency carers.

In February 2025 the Senedd passed a law that will remove private profit from children's residential and foster care in Wales, so in future care for looked-after children will be provided only by public, charitable or not-for-profit organisations. If you are comparing services, it is worth asking each one how this affects them.

Foster Wales Swansea says its fees and allowances are above the minimum rates set by the Welsh Government, with extra payments for birthdays, Christmas, holidays and religious festivals, and a weekly retainer for approved carers waiting to be matched. Carers have a supervising social worker, an out-of-hours support line, support groups (including groups for men who foster and for carers' own children), a buddy scheme and at least 15 hours of free training a year. You can start with weekends and school holidays and change your approval later.
Speak to the council and two or three of the services below before deciding which is right for you.

sources.title: Fostering with Swansea Council versus a fostering agency (Foster Wales Swansea)
